content: Masterwort typically refers to the plant Peucedanum ostruthium or Imperatoria ostruthium, which belongs to the family Apiaceae. It should not be confused with great masterwort, Astrantia major, which is also part of the same botanical family. This plant is commonly found in woodland gardens and meadows, particularly in areas that are semi-shaded. The roots of masterwort, which are harvested during the spring or fall, are known to possess a variety of medicinal properties. These include tonic, antiseptic, emmenagogue (stimulating menstrual flow), and diuretic effects. Traditionally, masterwort has been used to address issues such as flatulence, asthma, kidney and bladder stones, and water retention. Additionally, tea made from masterwort is believed to alleviate migraines and support the stimulation of the immune system.
